subject: MSA & Order Form — liability cap options and carve-outs
messages:
From: Simon Patel <simon@acme-analytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zac@acme-analytics.com>, contracts@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: initial MSA redlines — liability cap and consequential damages

Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving towards signature but legal flagged two items in the MSA/order form that are blocking procurement: the overall liability cap (they want a per-12-month reset rather than aggregate over the contract term) and a narrower carve-out for consequential damages (they want to preserve lost-revenue claims). I attached our redline (ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and highlighted the sections.

High level asks:
- Consider a rolling 12-month cap rather than a contractwide cap (ACME prefers this from a risk perspective).
- Exclude certain statutory and IP indemnity claims from the cap, but clarify consequential damage carve-outs.

Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility here and who on your side should own the discussion? Happy to hop on a short call.

Thanks,
Simon
Head of Procurement
Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: initial MSA redlines — liability cap and consequential damages

Simon —

Appreciate the redline and clear asks. Short answer: we can be flexible but need to balance commercial exposure with insurance and SLA economics. Proposed next steps:

1) Internal alignment: loop in Legal (Marissa) and Revenue (Karthik) to propose a set of concrete options.
2) Option set for Acme to choose from (we'll flag tradeoffs):
   • Annual rolling cap (12-month lookback) set at 2x trailing annual fees — good for customers with steady spend.
   • Contractwide aggregate cap = 3x total fees paid in the term (simpler for billing but can be larger exposure for long contracts).
   • Hybrid: per-billing-year cap with an overall hard stop (e.g., yearly cap = 1.5x fees that resets, but aggregate cap = 4x fees).
3) Consequential damages carve-out: we typically carve out IP indemnity, will consider narrowing consequential damage carve-outs to exclude only indirect prohibited categories (we need to confirm insurance position).

I'll get a legal redline and short memo with the tradeoffs today. If your team is free, let's do a 20-min call Wed morning PT to walk the options.

—Connor
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Simon Patel <simon@acme-analytics.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial MSA redlines — liability cap and consequential damages

Simon / Connor —

Looping in Legal and Contracts. Quick read of ACME's redline: the areas we should prioritize are the basis for the cap (fees paid vs. annualized fees), the reset mechanics, and a clear definition/exclusions list for consequential damages. A few notes from our side:

- Definitions: we need explicit language around "fees paid" (do we include credits/offsets, professional services, usage credits?). Recommend defining as "nett billings paid to Redwood for Services under this Order Form during the applicable measurement period."

- Annual vs. Aggregate:
   * Annual/rolling 12-month reset helps customers smooth exposure but increases our operational risk (billing spikes could create under-cap situations).
   * Contractwide aggregate cap simplifies enforcement and aligns with insurance limits.

- Multiples: market practice we're comfortable with: 2x-3x on annualized fees or 3x-6x on contract term depending on term length and expected run rate. For this deal size and ACME's profile, propose the following menu:
   Option A (customer-friendly): Rolling 12-month cap = 2.5x trailing 12-month fees; Consequential damages carved out only for statutory IP and willful misconduct.
   Option B (balanced): Per billing-year cap = 3x fees per year (resets at anniversary); Aggregate hard cap = 5x fees in the initial term; broader carve-outs limited to IP, indemnified claims, and fraud.
   Option C (commercially protective): Contractwide cap = 4x total fees paid in term; minimal carve-outs besides IP indemnity and statutory exclusions.

- Insurance check: I'll confirm with Risk about attachment to our umbrella policy; if insurance limits are low we may need to push customers towards Options B/C.

I'll attach a marked MSA with the three options and call out redline language for the Order Form. If Acme wants preferred language for an annual reset, propose a short clause that sets measurement periods to billing months aggregated to a rolling 12-month window.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial MSA redlines — liability cap and consequential damages

Simon —

Thanks for patience here. We reviewed the options and want to present a single implementable position to speed signature: Option B with a minor tweak. Key points:

- Final proposal: Per billing-year cap = 3x fees per year (resets at each anniversary). Aggregate hard cap = 5x total fees in the initial term. This balances Acme's desire for periodic relief and our need to bound lifetime exposure.
- Carve-outs: consequential damages remain excluded only for statutory and IP indemnity claims; lost revenue claims are allowed where tied to proven breach and up to the cap. We'll not accept an open-ended lost profits carve-out.
- Measurement: define "fees" as net billings actually paid (exclude credits and taxes). For usage variability, we'll use trailing 12 months for the first anniversary calculation.
- Implementation: Marissa to produce final redline language (including a one-paragraph explanation for procurement). Connor will confirm commercial acceptance and signoff authority for offered credits/commits.

If that works for Acme, we can circulate a final MSA and Order Form today for countersignature. Otherwise let's schedule 20 minutes to close.

Regards,
Karthik
Head of Revenue
Redwood Inference
